title: MCPoison: Cursor re-trusts an approved MCP server after its config changes
summary: Cursor bound MCP server approval to the server's name rather than its configuration, so once a project-level mcp.json entry had been approved an attacker with write access to the repository could swap in a different command and have it run silently on every subsequent open. Check Point Research reported it and Cursor fixed it in 1.3.
severity_rationale: Persistent, silent code execution for anyone who can land a commit in a shared repository, with no re-approval prompt.
